statement.excerpt: I don’t think any pure deep learning/big data system can match it.
statement.document_title: The New Science of Alt Intelligence

from_speaker: any pure deep learning/big data system
our_interpretation: The surrounding passage makes this a comparison with systems existing in May 2022, rather than a prediction of permanent impossibility.
I don't think qualifies the speaker's confidence; the assessable content is the capability comparison.
Match means comparable accuracy and task coverage on held-out spreadsheet string transformations after one user-provided example, with practical computational requirements.
Pure permits ordinary execution infrastructure but excludes a task-specific symbolic synthesis or verification engine supplying the transformation capability.
The target is May 2022 up to publication. Earlier comparisons are context and cannot establish the entire contemporary frontier.
criteria.support_condition: Broad, comparable tests show that the relevant pure neural systems available at the time fall materially below Flash Fill on one-example transformations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one qualifying system available at the time matches or exceeds Flash Fill on a representative one-example comparison.

evidence.explanation: The reported average-output comparison uses four demonstrations. It therefore cannot directly settle the one-example comparison inferred from Marcus's context.

The paper reports a synthesis model matching Flash Fill's clean-data accuracy in its four-example comparison, but the synthesized programs use deterministic execution. That result is relevant counterevidence to a broader dismissal of neural approaches, without establishing a qualifying pure one-example match.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reproducible one-example comparison between Flash Fill and qualifying pure neural systems available by May 14, 2022, with architecture, coverage, accuracy and computational requirements disclosed.
